newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Fin Minister sees foul play in Manila share fall.
newsitem.headline: Fin Minister sees foul play in Manila share fall.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Wednesday the recent share price collapse may have been orchestrated and urged market regulators to punish anyone found to have rigged prices.

In a statement, de Ocampo reiterated government insistence that there was no fundamental economic reason for the fall in share prices, which have slumped by about 16 percent since early April, initially on fears of an impending property collapse.

"(De Ocampo) suspects that rumours of a collapse in the property industry were planned to cause panic reaction, leading to the stock fall...there is good reason to suspect that the stock market behaviour in late April and early May was abnormal," his department said in a statement.
There was no reason for such a fall when both the market and the economy were sound, it quoted him as saying.
"(He) has ordered the Securities and Exchange Commission not to spare anybody and to use the full force of the law to rid the stock market of manipulators."
On Tuesday, the Philippines' SEC announced it had launched what it called a "discreet inquiry" into possible market rigging.
"De Ocampo said he is looking at the possibility of short-selling where some smart stock players make money from falling stock prices," the statement added.
